test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 11 Nov 2021 Shift 2
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

Madam Hooch asked the students what they were waiting for.

options.text: Madam Hooch said to the students, “What are you waiting for?”
Madam Hooch told the students, “What they were waiting for?”
The students said to Madam Hooch, “What are we waiting for?”
Madam Hooch said to the students, “What you are waiting for?”

solution:
The correct answer is:** Madam Hooch said to the students, “What are you waiting for?”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is a indirect speech and we need to convert it into an direct speech..
 
• We follow these rules in Direct-Indirect speech for an interrogative sentence:
 
 
• WH – question is formed with the use of who, which, when, where, how why.
 
• Yes-no question is formed with the use of auxiliary verbs such as – am, is, are, was, were, do, did, can, shall, will, have, has, may. 
 
• A question mark should always be used at the end of an interrogative sentence in direct speech.
 
• Ask is used as reporting verb instead of say, tell, say to. 
 
• The pronoun '**they**' changes to '**you**'.
 
• The Helping verb **were **changes to **was**.
 
• Interrogative sentence changes to assertive form [direct to indirect speech]
 
• After the conversion of an interrogative sentence from direct to indirect speech, the question mark changes to a full stop.
 
 
 
• Example - *The teacher asked me, “Why did not you come to school yesterday?” (Direct)*

* The teacher asked me why I had not come to school the previous day. (Indirect)*

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

Direct sentence: *Madam Hooch said to the students, “What are you waiting for?”*
